newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Nevada mountains get three metres of snow.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Nevada mountains get three metres of snow.

text.p: Residents of the Sierra Nevada began to dig out on Monday from a deadly storm that dumped up to 2.7 metres of snow, stranding thousands of travelers and knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes.

"It just kept on pouring in," said National Weather Service meteorologist Rick Canepa, adding that the amount of snowfall since Friday along the northern California-Nevada border may set a record for the Sierras.
Search teams rescued a young cross-country skier who was missing since Friday with his father in the Sierra Nevada mountains. The father, however, was found dead, authorities said.
The heavy snow also caused major transportation problems.
Amtrak's California Zephyr train, travelling from Chicago to Oakland, California, partially derailed in heavy snow and ice late on Sunday north of Sacramento.
None of the 118 passengers or crew was hurt, an Amtrak spokesman said. After several hours delay, the passengers were placed on buses to complete their trip.
Light snow continued to fall on Monday, but weather forecasters said the worst had past.
About 20,000 customers in the Sierra foothills remained without power late on Monday due to the heavy snowfall, power company spokeswoman Diane Sable said.

The heavy snow forced the closure of some highways through the mountains between California and Nevada. Road closures in the Lake Tahoe ski resort area stranded thousands of residents and travelers, South Lake Tahoe police dispatcher Sue Dickey said.
"Many cars were stranded, but the roads are improving," Dickey said.
Highways and roads buried by the snow were being cleared and many were reopened on Monday, allowing motorists to pass, the California Highway Patrol said.

Over the weekend, gusting winds from the powerful storm knocked down poles and power lines, causing scattered power outages along the northern California coast and causing problems for last-minute holiday shoppers and travelers.
Marble-size hail was reported in the San Francisco Bay area and Napa County officials said a small tornado touched down Sunday in wine country.
